A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, retaining the core UU-learning framework and classification experiments. The complete texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching content that was moved or merged.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on six datasets, including comparisons with other methods and appendix analyses of robust correction and class-prior estimation.

after.justification: v2 retains the original classification results and adds original experiments on generative safety alignment in Section 5.4 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: The iterative annotation, robust-UU training, and relabeling algorithm and its losses remain unchanged. v2 adds a downstream adaptation: the refined classifier supplies scalar rewards for PPO training of an Alpaca-fine-tuned generative policy (Section 5.4 and Appendix C.2).

E1.justification: The six classification datasets are retained. v2 adds Alpaca instruction-response data for supervised fine-tuning and uses Safety for response generation and policy alignment, substantially extending coverage beyond classifying existing examples.

E2.justification: The new alignment comparison adds an SFT-only policy and Vanilla RLAIF using a PN-trained reward model (Figure 4). Existing classification comparators remain unchanged; the UU comparator promoted into v2's main figure was already evaluated in v1's Appendix C.

E3.justification: The original classification splits, training settings, and accuracy evaluation are retained, including the 100-label setting already documented in v1's appendix. v2 introduces a distinct alignment protocol: one SFT epoch, four PPO epochs, a 128-token generation limit, and evaluation of generated responses using a reward model trained on correctly labeled Safety data.

E4.justification: The standard-UU versus robust-UU ablation and oracle/50-label/100-label comparisons already appear in v1's Appendix C and Figures 4–5. v2 consolidates these analyses into main Figures 2–3. The added alignment experiment supplies downstream benchmark evidence without a separate new robustness or sensitivity analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report classification results over three random seeds with mean and standard-deviation bands. The added alignment experiment also uses three seeds; its response-reward distributions and means introduce outcomes, without adding confidence intervals, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds alignment results absent from v1: Figure 4 reports mean rewards of 2.14 for SFT, 1.91 for Vanilla RLAIF, 5.96 for Ours (Oracle), and 5.91 for Ours (50-labeled), alongside reduced negative-reward mass for the proposed variants. Matched classification curves are unchanged; Tables 6–12 tabulate previously plotted results.

T1.justification: The mixture assumptions, risk definitions, weighting coefficients, and robust correction are retained. v1's displayed correction-function definition becomes inline text, and relabeling notation is condensed. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: v1 validates classification-label refinement and reserves LLM post-training for future work. v2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion add demonstrated generative safety alignment as a contribution, and RQ3 is redefined to address extension beyond classification.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the alignment results as evidence that more reliable reward signals improve policy optimization. Section 6 adds instance-level classifiability as a factor beyond initial label accuracy and discusses difficulty-guided curricula and auxiliary information. Existing noise and prior-estimation limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, dataset licensing/privacy information, and substantial SFT/PPO implementation and evaluator details in Appendix C.2 and Table 5. Original classifier details remain available. The new SFT batch size is inconsistent: Appendix C.2 states 16, while Table 5 states 64.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen et al.'s SAT work to the pseudo-labeling discussion and Taori et al.'s Alpaca reference for the new training stage. The positioning relative to UU learning, pseudo-labeling, and LLM self-refinement remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 updates the contribution summary, research questions, and conclusion, and compresses several lists and explanatory passages. The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact. Limitations move to Appendix A, and the appendices are reorganized and expanded.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Classification plots previously split between the main text and appendices are consolidated into Figures 2–3 with revised legends. v2 adds the alignment reward figure, baseline and alignment-parameter tables, and seven numerical-results tables, while reflowing the prompt panels.

improvement.justification: The controlled safety-alignment experiment provides useful evidence for the post-training application left untested in v1, using SFT and Vanilla RLAIF comparisons and an evaluator trained on correct labels. Added implementation details and numerical tables improve auditability. The gain is limited by the single Safety/1B-model setting, conflicting SFT batch sizes, and Appendix A's retained statement that post-training was not studied, which now contradicts Section 5.4.
